sources.title: Chronicle of Potosí
sources.author: Bartolomé Arzáns de Orsúa y Vela
sources.excerpt: This mountain of silver has consumed eight million Indian lives in its hellish mines.
sources.longExcerpt: Potosí, richest city in the Americas, built on a mountain of silver and indigenous blood. The Cerro Rico has yielded enough silver to build a bridge to Spain, they say. But at what cost? Eight million Indians have died in these mines, chewing coca leaves to survive the altitude, the cold, the sixteen-hour shifts. The city has 160,000 souls, 36 churches, 14 dance halls, 800 professional gamblers. Prices exceed those of Paris. A chicken costs eight reales, an Indian life is worth nothing.

citation.originalPublication: Bartolomé Arzáns de Orsúa y Vela, 1705

sources.title: Letter to King Manuel I
sources.author: Pero Vaz de Caminha
sources.excerpt: Esta terra, Senhor, me parece que da ponta que mais contra o sul vimos até à outra ponta que contra o norte vem, será tamanha que haverá nela vinte ou vinte e cinco léguas por costa. Os homens são pardos, maneira de avermelhados, de bons rostos e bons narizes.
sources.longExcerpt: Esta terra, Senhor, me parece que da ponta que mais contra o sul vimos até à outra ponta que contra o norte vem, será tamanha que haverá nela vinte ou vinte e cinco léguas por costa. Os homens são pardos, maneira de avermelhados, de bons rostos e bons narizes. This letter from 1500 represents the first written description of Brazil by the Portuguese, documenting the discovery of the land and first encounters with indigenous peoples.

sources.title: Royal Commentaries of the Incas
sources.author: Inca Garcilaso de la Vega
sources.excerpt: I was born in the great city of Cuzco, head and court of the kingdom and empire of Peru. My father was Spanish, and my mother was an Inca princess, daughter of Tupac Inca Yupanqui.
sources.longExcerpt: I was born in the great city of Cuzco, head and court of the kingdom and empire of Peru. My father was Spanish, and my mother was an Inca princess, daughter of Tupac Inca Yupanqui. This mestizo chronicler's work from 1609 provides a unique perspective on Inca history and culture, combining indigenous oral traditions with Spanish colonial documentation.

sources.title: Letters from Brazil
sources.author: José de Anchieta
sources.excerpt: Os gentios desta terra são muito numerosos e de várias nações e línguas. Vivem em aldeias com suas mulheres e filhos, sem rei nem lei, apenas seguindo seus costumes antigos.
sources.longExcerpt: Os gentios desta terra são muito numerosos e de várias nações e línguas. Vivem em aldeias com suas mulheres e filhos, sem rei nem lei, apenas seguindo seus costumes antigos. These letters from Jesuit missionary José de Anchieta provide detailed observations of indigenous Brazilian cultures in the 16th century, documenting languages, customs, and early missionary activities.

sources.title: La Araucana
sources.author: Alonso de Ercilla
sources.excerpt: No las damas, amor, no gentilezas de caballeros canto enamorados, ni las muestras, regalos y ternezas de amorosos afectos y cuidados, mas el valor, los hechos, las proezas de aquellos españoles esforzados.
sources.longExcerpt: No las damas, amor, no gentilezas de caballeros canto enamorados, ni las muestras, regalos y ternezas de amorosos afectos y cuidados, mas el valor, los hechos, las proezas de aquellos españoles esforzados. This epic poem from 1569 chronicles the Spanish conquest of Chile and the fierce resistance of the Mapuche people, written by a Spanish soldier who participated in the campaigns.

sources.title: History of the Imperial Villa of Potosí
sources.author: Bartolomé Arzáns de Orsúa
sources.excerpt: This mountain of silver has enriched the world and cost the lives of countless Indians who died extracting its treasures. The wealth flows to Spain while the workers perish in the depths.
sources.longExcerpt: This mountain of silver has enriched the world and cost the lives of countless Indians who died extracting its treasures. The wealth flows to Spain while the workers perish in the depths. This chronicle from 1705 documents the brutal reality of colonial silver mining in Potosí, Bolivia, one of the richest and deadliest mining operations in history.
